rules.title: Which words can you use?
rules.paraphrase: Write only with dictionary-approved words, technical nouns, and technical verbs.

rules.title: Part of speech
rules.paraphrase: Give an approved word only the part of speech the dictionary assigns it.

rules.title: Approved meaning
rules.paraphrase: Give an approved word only its listed meaning.

rules.title: Forms of verbs and adjectives
rules.paraphrase: Use only the verb and adjective forms that the dictionary lists.

rules.title: Technical nouns
rules.paraphrase: A noun that fits one of the listed technical-noun categories may be used.

technical_noun_categories: Vehicles or machines, and locations on them
Tools and support equipment, their parts, and locations on them
Systems, components and circuits, their functions, configurations, and parts
Mathematical, scientific, engineering terms, and formulas
Numbers, units of measurement and time (and their symbols)
Professional roles, individuals, groups, organizations, and geopolitical entities
Common personal effects, food, and beverages
Official documents, parts of documentation, standards, and guidelines
Computer science, information and communication technology
Animals, plants, and other life forms

rules.title: Technical nouns
rules.paraphrase: An unapproved word is acceptable only as a technical noun or inside one.

rules.title: Technical nouns
rules.paraphrase: Never turn a technical noun into a verb.

rules.title: Technical nouns
rules.paraphrase: Take technical nouns from those your organization or field already accepts.

rules.title: Technical nouns
rules.paraphrase: Pick technical nouns that are brief and plain.

rules.title: Technical nouns
rules.paraphrase: Keep regional words, slang, and jargon out of technical nouns.

rules.title: Technical nouns
rules.paraphrase: Name one item with one technical noun throughout.

rules.title: Technical verbs
rules.paraphrase: A verb that fits one of the listed technical-verb categories may be used.

technical_verb_categories: Instructions and information for applicable subject fields

rules.title: Technical verbs
rules.paraphrase: Never turn a technical verb into a noun.

rules.title: Spelling
rules.paraphrase: Spell the American way unless a governing directive says otherwise.

rules.title: Multi-word nouns
rules.paraphrase: Keep each multi-word noun to three words or fewer.

rules.title: Multi-word nouns
rules.paraphrase: Write a technical noun longer than three words in full first, then shorten or hyphenate it.

rules.title: Verb forms and tenses of verbs
rules.paraphrase: Use a verb only in the forms that its dictionary entry gives.

rules.title: Verb forms and tenses of verbs
rules.paraphrase: Limit verbs to the infinitive, imperative, simple present, simple past, simple future, and the past participle used as an adjective.

rules.title: Verb forms and tenses of verbs
rules.paraphrase: Use a past participle only as an adjective.

rules.title: Verb forms and tenses of verbs
rules.paraphrase: Do not stack auxiliary verbs into compound tenses.

rules.title: Verb forms and tenses of verbs
rules.paraphrase: Allow an -ing word only as a technical noun, a modifier inside one, or one of the few approved -ing words.

rules.title: Active voice
rules.paraphrase: Write in the active voice; descriptive text may use the passive only when the agent is unknown.

rules.title: How to describe an action
rules.paraphrase: Show an action with an approved verb, not a noun or other word class.

rules.title: Short sentences and clear sentence structures
rules.paraphrase: Keep sentences short and their structure clear.

rules.title: Short sentences and clear sentence structures
rules.paraphrase: Write every word in full: no dropped words and no contractions.

rules.title: Vertical lists
rules.paraphrase: Put complex content into a vertical list.

rules.title: Connecting words and connecting phrases
rules.paraphrase: Join sentences on related topics with connecting words or phrases.

rules.title: Articles and demonstrative adjectives
rules.paraphrase: Put an article or a demonstrative adjective before a noun where one fits.

rules.title: Sentences
rules.paraphrase: In procedures, keep each sentence to 20 words or fewer; notes in procedures may reach 25.

rules.title: Sentences
rules.paraphrase: Give one instruction per sentence unless the actions happen at the same time.

rules.title: Verbs in procedures
rules.paraphrase: Phrase instructions as commands.

rules.title: Descriptive statements in instructions
rules.paraphrase: Open an instruction with any condition the reader needs first, set off from the command by a comma.

rules.title: Notes
rules.paraphrase: Use notes for information only, never for instructions.

rules.title: Content structure
rules.paraphrase: Present information step by step.

rules.title: Content structure
rules.paraphrase: Structure the text with key words and key phrases.

rules.title: Sentences
rules.paraphrase: In descriptive text, keep each sentence to 25 words or fewer.

rules.title: Paragraphs
rules.paraphrase: Group related information into paragraphs.

rules.title: Paragraphs
rules.paraphrase: Give each paragraph a single topic.

rules.title: Paragraphs
rules.paraphrase: Keep each paragraph to six sentences or fewer.

rules.title: How to write safety instructions
rules.paraphrase: Mark the level of risk with a signal word such as warning or caution.

rules.title: How to write safety instructions
rules.paraphrase: Begin a safety instruction with a clear command or condition.

rules.title: How to write safety instructions
rules.paraphrase: Explain the risk or the possible result.

rules.title: Punctuation
rules.paraphrase: Any standard English punctuation is allowed except the semicolon.

rules.title: Punctuation
rules.paraphrase: Hyphenate words that belong together directly.

rules.title: Punctuation
rules.paraphrase: Parentheses serve references, identifiers, step numbers, abbreviations, singular-plural pairs, explanations, and alternatives.

rules.title: Word count
rules.paraphrase: In a vertical list, a colon ends a sentence for word count, and each list item counts as its own sentence.

rules.title: Word count
rules.paraphrase: Text in parentheses counts as one word of its sentence and as a sentence of its own.

rules.title: Word count
rules.paraphrase: Count a number, number with unit, abbreviation, alphanumeric identifier, quotation, title, or proper noun as one word.

rules.title: Word count
rules.paraphrase: Count a hyphenated word as one word.

rules.title: Different sentence constructions
rules.paraphrase: Recast the sentence when swapping words one for one is not enough.

rules.title: How to use approved words correctly
rules.paraphrase: Use every approved word correctly.

rules.title: How to use approved words correctly
rules.paraphrase: Do not build phrasal verbs from two words.

rules.title: Consistent style
rules.paraphrase: Keep terminology and wording consistent.
